title: Advice for a New Student at WKU
writingModel: Advice for a New Student at WKU — by Kamila Seitkali

Dear new student, welcome to WKU. I've been here for three years now, and I'd like to share some things I wish someone had told me on my first day. Some of these are rules you must follow. Others are advice — things I think you should do to have a genuinely good experience here.

First, the rules. You must attend at least 80% of every course. This is non-negotiable — missing more than 20% means automatic failure, regardless of your exam result. You also mustn't plagiarise. This includes copying from the internet, submitting another student's work, and using AI tools to write your assignments. The consequences are serious. I strongly recommend reading the academic integrity section of the student handbook in your first week.

Second, the practical advice. You should check your email every single day. The university sends important information there — deadlines, room changes, notifications about results. If you miss an email, you miss the information, and that's nobody's fault but your own. You also ought to speak to your academic adviser at least once per semester. They're there to help you.

Third, the things you don't need to worry about. You don't have to buy every book on the reading list — the library has most of them, and many are available online. You needn't memorise every rule from day one — the handbook is always available. And you don't have to know exactly what you want from your degree when you arrive. That comes with time.

In my experience, the most important thing is not to isolate yourself. You should talk to your classmates, join at least one student club, and ask for help when you need it. The student support office exists precisely for people who feel lost. You needn't go through any of this alone.

One last thing: be kind to yourself. You must take your obligations seriously, but you shouldn't expect to be perfect from day one. You're going to make mistakes — that's what learning looks like. What matters is that you keep going.
Good luck. WKU is a good place. Use it well.
